questions.question: Taxis. I'm in Marrakesh and need taxi from Riad in Medina to bus station. Riad wants 20 euro but booking dot com only wants 5 euro. If I book online or get an Uber, will taxi find me at my riad if no cars able to drive directly?
questions.trip_context: Currently in Marrakesh, riad inside the medina, needs to reach the bus station
questions.source_response: Karyn: "Download inDrive.. it's like Uber.."; Lucas: "Taxis are everywhere. Just hail one. 50 dirhams gets you there (even if they should use their meter but don't... alas... that's a... [truncated in source]"
questions.extracted_advice: Either use the inDrive app, which works like Uber, or simply hail a street taxi; one traveller reports paying around 50 dirhams for this trip and notes meters are often not used.
questions.key_facts: inDrive named as an app option. 50 dirhams quoted by one traveller for a medina-to-bus-station taxi. Meters exist but are frequently not used. The riad quoted 20 euro versus 5 euro online.

questions.must_not_do: Do not present 50 dirhams as a fixed fare. Do not ignore the actual question, which is whether a booked car can reach a medina riad at all.
questions.natural_answer_requirement: Address the medina access problem directly, because that is the real issue behind the question, and explain agreeing the fare up front.
questions.evaluation_notes: Flagship test: does the AI understand medina taxi access limitations and treat a reported fare as anecdotal?

source_examples.why_it_matters: Shows the structure a strong answer takes: name the two real options, name the operators, and give an indicative price range without pretending it is fixed.

source_examples.question: Trying to figure out how much money I need to exchange. What can I expect to pay for an average meal?
source_examples.response: Jane: "Firstly I changed GBP100 and I was on my own. That lasted me almost the full week for food and the odd beer." Anonymous: "We changed 100 euros each for three and a half days. Got back to the airport and had plenty of change."
source_examples.why_it_matters: The clearest anecdote-versus-fact trap in the dataset. Both answers are useful and both would become false if restated as general cost guidance.

source_examples.question: I am arriving in Casablanca on 1 October and plan to go to Essaouira directly. Can anyone recommend a taxi service which is safe for a solo woman?
source_examples.response: Simon: "A private driver to Essaouira is a waste of money. I'm not poor. I still took CTM. You could take the train to Marrakech and t..." Katie: "Take a bus from CTM to Essaouira, will be cheap and safe"
source_examples.why_it_matters: A directly stated personal preference with the reasoning attached. The AI should be able to relay the preference without converting it into a rule that CTM beats private drivers.

source_examples.question: I'm trying to work out what the weather will be like in Marrakech in early November so I know what to pack, but I've been told everything from mad hot to wet and even chilly.

source_examples.why_it_matters: A model of honest uncertainty: the community refuses to invent a forecast and gives advice that works either way. This is the tone ComeMorocco should adopt on weather questions.

Reda: "People have to understand that intestinal flora is different from country to country. Therefore it's wise to buy bottled water"
source_examples.why_it_matters: Two answers that look contradictory but are not. A good ComeMorocco answer reconciles them instead of choosing one, and avoids the reflexive 'don't drink the water' line a local pushes back on.

source_examples.response: GentlePenguino457: "That way you are going to be in the car most of the time. You should have at least 2 weeks for this. I really don't get this w..." Harvey: "That seems like a lot of ground to cover in 6 days if you want to stop at all these places"

source_examples.why_it_matters: Local geographic knowledge correcting a media-driven worry. It also shows why on-the-ground reassurance must never be recycled as current information.

source_examples.question: My wife wants to know if she could buy some nice tops at the souks that she could wear to dinner.
source_examples.response: Anonymous: "I've never found decent clothes in the souks for women. They have a lot of football kits and fake designer stuff but it's mos..." Wendy: "I was hoping the same thing and I didn't find anything that I would feel comfortable wearing"
source_examples.why_it_matters: Honest expectation correction. The helpful answer here is the disappointing one, and ComeMorocco needs to be willing to give it.

source_examples.question: I am a huge dog lover and would love to give back by handing out small goodie bags to local children containing cookies, candy, small toys and 20 dirhams. Is this well-received?
source_examples.response: Anonymous: "Please please do not give goodie bags to kids...they then see all motorhomes as something they can beg from..." PurpleReindeer594: "You can donate to local animal sanctuaries or shelters. For kids, I do not recommend giving them mo..."
source_examples.why_it_matters: Responsible-travel guidance that respects a good intention while redirecting it. Note that another post in the same source recommends bringing chocolate for children, which is exactly the kind of contradiction the dataset must capture.

source_examples.question: I was quoted 120 euros for a half day English tour guide in Marrakech. Is this a normal price?
source_examples.response: Gabriella: "That sounds quite high. 50-60 EUR is more normal" Jawad: "For a half day, 4 hours, should be between 50 and 70 max but 120 is too much."
source_examples.why_it_matters: Two independent price benchmarks that agree. Useful because it shows the AI can give a helpful ballpark while still labelling it as community benchmark rather than published rate.

source_examples.question: Me and my friend (Americans) traveled through Morocco a couple of weeks ago, 16 days in total. I've had some time to reflect on the trip and thought I'd offer some thoughts as I had many of the same safety concerns and questions that a lot of people in this group have. We visited Marrakech, Imlil, Fez, Chaouen, Safi and Essaouira via domestic flight, bus, train and taxi.
source_examples.response: "My main takeaway from the trip is that I shouldn't have waited... [truncated in source]" - a widely engaged reflective post from a traveller who had shared the group's common safety worries before going.
source_examples.why_it_matters: The single most-engaged post in the source. It shows the register travellers actually trust: reflective, specific about routes and transport used, and honest about having been anxious beforehand.

source_examples.question: Just came back from beautiful Morocco. Here are my tips, we were 3 women traveling.
source_examples.response: "1: Taxi from Casablanca airport to hotel (45 min drive) is maximum 300 dirham. If you want to give a tip then 30 dirham is enough... 2: Watch out for scammers: red taxi in Casablanca is for a 10 min drive about 20 dirham. 15 min drive about 30 dirham. So if they say 150, just search for another."
source_examples.why_it_matters: Highly practical, numbered, specific. This is the format travellers reward. It is also a reminder that the numbers are one trip's experience, not a tariff, and a second traveller independently confirming the 300 dirham airport fare does not make it a fixed rate.

source_examples.question: I would love to visit Morocco with my girlfriend but we are two women and my girlfriend is masculine in appearance. She fears it will not be safe for her.
source_examples.response: Autumn: "Modest clothing and no public affection are a part of Moroccan culture, regardless of whether you are straight or gay/queer." Mo: "I am Moroccan and can definitely say that you're safe in Morocco. 3 things are important to notice: conservative sh..."
source_examples.why_it_matters: A sensitive question answered with respect and without either alarm or false promises. The reframing that public affection norms apply to everyone is the key move a good answer should reproduce.

source_examples.question: I have been quoted $130 USD a night for a riad in Marrakech. Is this a reasonable price to pay?
source_examples.response: Don: "Without a description, how could anyone offer a reasonable opinion?"
source_examples.why_it_matters: A useful reminder that some questions cannot be answered as asked. The right response identifies the missing information rather than inventing an average.
